value.body: The Engineering Services Examination (ESE), often still called IES, is run by UPSC to recruit Group A engineers into central government departments such as railways, central engineering services, defence engineering, telecom and others. It covers four branches: Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, and Electronics & Telecommunication engineering.

items.label: Stages
items.note: Prelims is objective; Mains is descriptive (conventional) papers

items.label: Age limit
items.note: Relaxation for reserved categories and certain government servants

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A degree in engineering (B.E. / B.Tech or equivalent, including AMIE sections A & B), or an M.Sc in certain subjects (wireless communication, electronics, radio physics) for the E&T stream. Final-year students can apply provisionally. The notification usually comes out around September; prelims follows early the next year and mains around mid-year.

value.title: At a glance
items: The pool is smaller than Civil Services, but seats are also few — a few hundred a year across four branches — so selection rates are low.
Prelims includes a common General Studies & Engineering Aptitude paper plus a branch paper; preparation overlaps strongly with GATE.
Vacancy numbers vary a lot from year to year, partly depending on whether railway (IRMS) posts are recruited through ESE.
Service allocation depends on rank, preference and the vacancies each department reports.

value.title: ESE vacancies at notification, by exam year
value.note: Vacancies as first notified; UPSC and the ministries often revise the final number later. Each exam year's notice is issued in the preceding September.
value.source: UPSC ESE notifications for each year (as reported by Scroll, Careers360 and other outlets)
